text:
lee: Hit a confusing repro during onboarding: when a project key rotates, the SDK's retry layer keeps using an old env key for in-flight batches and then switches mid-stream to the org-default returned by metadata. Users saw mixed-tenant requests.

maya: can you paste short repro?

lee: repro: set REDWOOD_API_KEY=pk_local_old, REDWOOD_PROJECT=team-1. start sample app that sends batched requests. rotate project key in metadata to pk_org_new. some requests succeed (old key) then later ones succeed under org tenant. logs show alternating tenant ids.

harry: that smells like caching + credential resolver order. the retry/batcher keeps a cached credential instance and we mutate which key the resolver points to when metadata changes.

sasha: ouch. we should never mutate a credentials object mid-request. expected behavior: a single request (including retries) should use the same effective credential sourced at start time, and env/flag should take precedence over metadata.

dev-bot: created issue DEVEX-4002: credential churn during batching causes cross-tenant requests. Link: internal/DEVEX-4002

maya: quick mitigation: make the batcher snapshot the effective key at request start. longer term: fix resolver precedence so env var/flag wins and avoid swapping cached cred references when project metadata changes.

lee: also add a small debug print in sampleapp: show effective key source per process and per worker thread. would help reproduce.

harry: tests: unit test for batcher snapshot behavior, integration for rotation where metadata changes mid-batch, and an e2e with sampleapp.

sasha: also add `rw auth:whoami --format=short` output and a `--lock` flag for the SDK which pins credential resolution for the lifetime of a request. Docs should recommend `--lock` for long-running batched workloads.

maya: will open PR: 1) batcher snapshots creds, 2) resolver checks env/flag before metadata, 3) add whoami CLI, 4) add telemetry event when fallback to org default occurs. small changelog and sampleapp README update.

dev-bot: maya/fix/batch-cred-stability opened PR #1209  CI: 5 checks queued

lee: thanks all. this one caused a customer demo to look like requests belonged to two tenants. locking creds per-request + clearer precedence should fix onboarding confusion.

sasha: and add a one-liner warning when config looks like "env key + REDWOOD_PROJECT" recommending explicit --api-key during local dev.

maya: will include that in the README and add a docs blurb. ping here when green.

harry: :thumbsup
